t: A great principality of southern France, ruled by the Raymondine counts of Toulouse from the ninth century until 1271.
Its courts patronised the troubadours, and Count Raymond IV led a major army on the First Crusade that founded the County of Tripoli.
The Albigensian Crusade against the Cathars broke the counts, and the county passed to the French crown in 1271.
dyk: Simon de Montfort, leader of the Albigensian Crusade, was killed in 1218 by a stone from a siege engine outside Toulouse; an Occitan chronicle says women of the city worked the machine.
ev: Charlemagne appoints Chorson as count of Toulouse
Raymond IV leaves for the First Crusade at the head of the southern army
Raymond IV’s son Bertrand takes Tripoli, founding the County of Tripoli
Henry II of England besieges Toulouse but withdraws
The Albigensian Crusade begins with the massacre at Béziers
Simon de Montfort defeats Raymond VI and Peter II of Aragon at Muret
The Treaty of Paris marries Raymond VII’s heiress to Alphonse of Poitiers
The county passes to the French crown

f.founder: Chorson (first count, appointed by Charlemagne); hereditary line from Fredelo and Raymond I
